question.worked_solution:
First, we convert the integrand into a sum of partial fractions:

$$
\frac{9x-38}{(4-x)^{2}(2-x)}=\frac{A}{(4-x)}+\frac{B}{(4-x)^{2}}+\frac{C}{(2-x)}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,$ $B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(4-x)^{2}(2-x)$ and get

$$
9x-38=A(4-x)(2-x)+B(2-x)+C(4-x)^{2}.
$$

Plugging in $x=4,$ we can eliminate $A$ and $C$ and solve for $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}9(4)-38 & =A(4-4)(2-4)+B(2-4)+C(4-4)^{2} \\ 36-38 & =B(-2) \\ B & =\frac{-2}{-2} \\ B & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=2,$ we can eliminate $A$ and $B$ and solve for $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}9(2)-38 & =A(4-2)(2-2)+B(2-2)+C(4-2)^{2} \\ 18-38 & =C{(2)}^{2} \\ C & =\frac{-20}{4} \\ C & =-5\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=0$ and substituting the known values of $B$ and $C,$ we can solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}9(0)-38 & =A(4-0)(2-0)+B(2-0)+C(4-0)^{2} \\ -38 & =8A+2B+16C \\ -38 & =8A+2(1)+16(-5) \\ -38 & =8A-78 \\ 8A & =78-38 \\ A & =\frac{40}{8} \\ A & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{9x-38}{(4-x)^{2}(2-x)}=\frac{5}{(4-x)}+\frac{1}{(4-x)^{2}}-\frac{5}{(2-x)}.
$$

Finally, we integrate this expression term by term, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{9x-38}{(4-x)^{2}(2-x)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{5}{(4-x)}+\frac{1}{(4-x)^{2}}-\frac{5}{(2-x)})\,\text{d}x \\  & =5\int \frac{1}{4-x}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{(4-x)^{2}}\,\text{d}x-5\int \frac{1}{2-x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-5\operatorname{ln}⁡|4-x|+\frac{1}{4-x}+5\operatorname{ln}⁡|2-x|+K,\end{aligned}
$$

where $K$ is an integral constant.
